lines.text: Quebec's Cape Diamond holds no diamonds.
In 1541, the French explorer Jacques Cartier made his third voyage.
lines.say: In fifteen forty one, the French explorer Zhahk Kar tee ay made his third voyage.

lines.text: His colonists settled near today's Quebec City.
There they picked up glittering stones they took for diamonds.
They also found rock that looked like gold.
In France, the diamonds proved to be quartz crystals.
The gold turned out to be iron pyrite.
France even made a saying: as false as a Canadian diamond.
The cliff above Quebec City is called Cape Diamond for those stones.
The Citadel of Quebec now stands on it, about 100 meters up.
lines.say: The Citadel of Quebec now stands on it, about one hundred meters up.
